 NBA Insider Chris B. Haynes reports that Ja Morant will start alongside Damian Lillard in Portland’s backcourt to open the 2026-27 season. 
 Conflicting offseason reports noted that Morant could come off the bench, but the Blazers will play the pair of superstar guards together in Wednesday’s season opener against the Suns. Fantasy managers should pay close attention to this pairing and keep in mind that Portland may experiment with different lineups throughout the season.
 -  Zak Hanshew 
 Source:  Chris B. Haynes

 Trail Blazers will start Ja Morant, Damian Lillard, Deni Avdija, Toumani Camara and Donovan Clingan against the Suns on Wednesday. 
 Lillard will be back on the floor for the first time in over a year after missing all of last season with an Achilles injury. He’ll also be back in a Trail Blazers uniform for the first time since the 2022-23 season. Lillard will start alongside Morant, Avdija, Camara and Clingan. 
 Ja Morant 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #1 
 Ja Morant tallied 19 points (8-of-10 FGs), three rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Friday’s exhibition against the Warriors. 
 Morant had a good night shooting the basketball, making 80 percent of his attempts and all three of his three-pointers. He finished with more turnovers (four) than assists (three), but fantasy managers likely know Morant will have some high-turnover nights. More importantly, he stays healthy, as the athletic point guard has had at least one extended absence throughout his career. Availability and efficiency concerns have hurt Morant’s ADP, as he’ll be more valuable to managers willing to punt turnovers. 
 Damian Lillard 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Damian Lillard accounted for 23 points (4-of-10 FGs, 13-of-13 FTs), one rebound, one assist and two three-pointers in Friday’s exhibition against the Warriors. 
 Based on Friday’s starting lineup, fantasy managers can assume (if they haven’t already) that the Trail Blazers will start Lillard and Ja Morant together to begin the regular season. Both took 10 field-goal attempts against the Warriors, and Lillard also got 13 free-throw attempts. However, in the 22:29 they shared the court, Portland posted a net rating of minus-20.6. Lillard’s offensive production won’t be an issue, but defensive concerns may force head coach Micah Nori to stagger Lillard and Morant’s minutes more than he did on Friday. 
 Ja Morant 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #1 
 Ja Morant came off the bench on Tuesday and finished with 14 points (4-of-6 FGs, 6-of-9 FTs), two rebounds, six assists and one steal against the Kings. 
 Trail Blazers head coach Micah Nori has been toying with the starting lineup in the preseason, with Damian Lillard and Scoot Henderson starting in this game, while Morant and Jrue Holiday came off the bench. Morant was still productive, and it’s clear the four guards will all have a significant role. Morant and Holiday will reportedly start in their next preseason game, and the starting unit for opening night still hasn’t been decided. 
 Jrue Holiday 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Jrue Holiday finished Monday’s exhibition against the London Lions with six points (3-of-5 FGs), five rebounds and three assists. 
 Damian Lillard didn’t play in Monday’s exhibition, and his absence opened a starting spot for Holiday. Like the other starters, the veteran guard was done at halftime. The move to the bench lowers Holiday’s fantasy ceiling considerably, giving managers no reason to use a top-100 pick on him. However, he should play enough to provide reliable late-round value in most leagues. 
 Ja Morant 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #1 
 Ja Morant tallied eight points (3-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, five assists and two steals in Wednesday’s exhibition against the Warriors. 
 Making his unofficial Trail Blazers debut, Morant logged 19 minutes and recorded five assists. By comparison, the other four starters combined for six helpers. He didn’t score much, but that shouldn’t concern fantasy managers. The concern is Morant’s availability, as managers should assume at least one extended injury absence. After appearing in at least 61 games in three of his first four seasons, Morant has played 79 games over the last three. That concern knocks him down most draft boards, regardless of league format. 
 Damian Lillard 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Damian Lillard finished Wednesday’s exhibition against the Warriors with 15 points (5-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), one rebound, one assist, two steals and three three-pointers. 
 Appearing in a game for the first time since the 2025 NBA Playoffs, Lillard looked sharp in his 19 minutes. Coming off a ruptured Achilles tendon, he started alongside newcomer Ja Morant and did most of his work off the ball. Lillard will be a key figure for the Trail Blazers this season, but his assist production may take a slight hit with Morant’s arrival. That said, Lillard simply being on the court is a win for fantasy managers and basketball in general. 
 Damian Lillard 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #0 
 Damian Lillard (Achilles) has no restrictions going into training camp. 
 Lillard, who did not play last season while recovering from a ruptured Achilles tendon, was cleared to resume 5-on-5 in late April, so his statement at Trail Blazers media day is not a surprise. Lillard said that he’s “operating like I wasn’t hurt,” which is music to the ears of fantasy managers. However, one concern as he begins his second stint in Portland is the team’s perimeter depth. The Trail Blazers acquired Ja Morant from Memphis, and they also have holdovers Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. That may lead to Lillard’s workload being managed early in the season, potentially lowering his fantasy ceiling. 
 D'Angelo Russell 
 WAS 
 Guard 
 #28 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that the Grizzlies are acquiring D’Angelo Russell from the Wizards in a trade. 
 The details from the reported six-team trade are still unfolding, but what’s already known is that Russell is heading to Memphis. The veteran guard had a tough 2025-26 season, playing just 26 total games with the Mavericks before being traded to the Wizards and never logging a minute for Washington. He’ll likely have a chance to play decent minutes for a Grizzlies team that recently traded away its superstar point guard, Ja Morant. If so, Russell could have some value in fantasy leagues this upcoming season. 
 Ja Morant 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #12 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that the Grizzlies have traded Ja Morant to the Trail Blazers for Jerami Grant and Kris Murray. 
 The second overall pick in the 2019 draft, Morant’s time in Memphis has come to an end. While there were certainly high points, most notably his winning Rookie of the Year in 2020 and making two All-Star teams, the inability to stay healthy and off-court issues ultimately led the Grizzlies to seek a way to move on. Morant appeared in 20 games last season, averaging 19.5 points, 3.3 rebounds, 8.1 assists, 1.0 steals and 1.0 three-pointers. With the Trail Blazers having Damian Lillard and Jrue Holiday on the roster, it’s fair to wonder if this will be Morant’s final destination. He’ll likely need a move to a third team to protect his fantasy ceiling in 2026-27.

 Kyrie Irving had 15 points (6-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, one steal and one three-pointer against the Rockets on Wednesday. 
 Irving was limited to just 23 minutes against the Rockets Wednesday as he was returning from injury. The 34-year-old point guard missed all of last season with a torn ACL and a calf strain. Irving still scored 15 points on nine attempts in those 23 minutes. Expect his minutes and production to increase as the Mavericks ease him into the beginning of the regular season.

 Cooper Flagg had 32 points (10-of-17 FGs, 11-of-13 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, three steals, one block and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s game against the Rockets. 
 Flagg filled up the stat sheet and dropped 32 points in the Mavericks season opener. There’s not much more you could ask from the 19-year-old, which shows how much of an uphill battle it might be for Dallas this year as the Mavericks lost to the Rockets by 18. Flagg and the Mavericks have two more games this week with a back-to-back against the Pacers and Spurs on Friday and Saturday.

 Oso Ighodaro (hip) will not return to Wednesday’s game against the Trail Blazers. 
 Ighodaro took a hit to his right hip during the second quarter of Wednesday’s game. Although he initially tried to play through the injury, the 7-footer was subbed out with just over a minute left in the half. Ighodaro didn’t return to the bench for the third quarter, and he’s done for the night. Khaman Maluach, who started Wednesday’s game, should play more minutes while Duop Reath slides into the back end of the rotation.

 Alperen Şengün had 23 points (9-of-15 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 10 rebounds, five assists and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s game against the Mavericks. 
 Şengün didn’t record any blocks or steals in this one, but he was +23 in 29 minutes as the Rockets won by 18. The 24-year-old center had a double-double with 23 points and 10 rebounds. He also made both of his three-point attempts. After a what was considered a down-year for him last year, Şengün got off to a good start this season.

 Kevin Durant had 30 points (10-of-16 FGs, 8-of-11 FTs), six rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in the Rockerts’ 128-110 victory over the Mavericks on Wednesday. 
 Durant started his 19th season in the NBA off with an excellent performance. The 38-year-old forward dropped 30 points on 16 attempts as the Rockets won going away over the Mavericks. Durant played 37 minutes after averaging 36.3 minutes last season. While the Rockets’ top brass has talked about managing his minutes, Durant wasn’t held back at all in the season opener.

 Davion Mitchell produced 11 points (4-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 10 assists, one block and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
 The good news for fantasy managers was that Mitchell recorded a double-double, which included a game-high 10 assists. However, for category-league managers, the six turnovers hurt. Mitchell logged 33 minutes in Wednesday’s opener, with Pelle Larsson (two points, three rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block) taking on the playmaking responsibilities when “Off Night” was on the bench. Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo can also initiate the offense, and they’ll likely need to because Miami lacks depth at point guard.

 Klay Thompson notched 10 points (3-of-6 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), one rebound and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
 After making two of his three three-point attempts and scoring six points in the first quarter, Thompson did not provide much value in his official Heat debut. While starting was a positive for the veteran guard, he played just 16 minutes. Meanwhile, Tim Hardaway Jr. (three points, four rebounds, one assist, one steal and one three-pointer) logged 18 minutes off the bench. Outside of deep leagues where you need three-pointers, you gain little by rostering Thompson.

 Murray filled up the stat sheet in the loss to the Pacers Wednesday.  Bam Adebayo posted 15 points (6-of-12 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, three steals and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
 After scoring six points on 3-of-9 shooting in the first half, Adebayo scored nine in the third quarter. Unfortunately for fantasy managers, the Heat center went scoreless in the fourth, attempting just one shot. The on-court chemistry between Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo needs work, which isn’t a surprise. But at times, Bam looked like little more than a bystander on offense, and that can’t happen.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo tallied 35 points (13-of-19 FGs, 9-of-14 FTs), six rebounds, one assist and one steal in Wednesday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
 Giannis came out hot in his official Heat debut, scoring 14 points in the first quarter. He went into the halftime break with 21, but no other Heat player scored more than seven. Antetokounmpo finished with a solid stat line, but fantasy managers may have hoped for more on the defensive end. The Heat host the Pistons Friday in the first of two games in as many nights before visiting Charlotte on Saturday.
